environment.oxipix_next_source: oxipix imgproc, git branch OXI-96-imgproc-wave-3 (stacked on OXI-94 and OXI-95)

benchmarks.warning_note: oximedia-cv's SSIM (15.4x slower than pure Rust separable SSIM, 32.6x slower than OpenCV) runs a non-separable 2D 11x11 window loop with per-tap bounds checks per pixel instead of 5 separable 1D passes (cool-japan/oximedia#31).

oximedia-cv's FastDetector misses corners whose 9-pixel arc wraps around the ring (1424 corners against 2091 in OpenCV and 2204 in imageproc), so its time is for less work. Known difference, see PERF_QUEUE.md.

oximedia-cv's FastDetector (about 7 ms) is about 3x slower than imageproc's oriented FAST (about 2 ms) on the same 868x600 photo. Tracked in the perf queue under feature_detection_fast and feature_description.

benchmarks.operation: FAST + BRIEF matching (t=20, 250 kp, up to 32 bits)

benchmarks.warning_note: The oxipix threshold helper runs a per-pixel GrayImage::from_fn wrapper over otsu_threshold (~3.6x slower than imageproc's tight slice loop; native slice thresholding tracked in OXI-89).

oximedia-cv erode is 11.4x slower than imageproc (335x slower than OpenCV) because StructuringElement::iter_active recomputes (i % w, i / w) offsets and checks bounds per tap with no separable rectangular fast path (cool-japan/oximedia#30).

oximedia-cv top_hat is 33.8x slower than imageproc (507x slower than OpenCV) for a 7x7 square window due to non-separable 2D erode/dilate with per-pixel iter_active() coordinate division and bounds checks (cool-japan/oximedia#30).

oximedia-cv GaussianBlur is 2.7x slower than image::imageops::blur (23.9x slower than OpenCV) due to per-channel plane splitting and generic 2D/separable float passes without integer SIMD vectorisation (cool-japan/oximedia#29).

Median 5x5 is 41.0x (imageproc) to 90.0x (oximedia-cv) slower than OpenCV: oximedia-cv heap-allocates a Vec and calls sort_unstable() at every pixel instead of using a 256-bin sliding histogram (cool-japan/oximedia#29, OXI-93).

oximedia-cv bilateral filter is 3.6x slower than imageproc (41.5x slower than OpenCV): it runs 3 grayscale passes in f64 calling f64::exp() inside the 4-deep loop without a 256-entry range LUT (cool-japan/oximedia#29, OXI-93).

Pure Rust imageproc Sobel X is ~4.9x slower than oximedia-cv (27.2x slower than OpenCV) because horizontal_sobel allocates an intermediate i16 buffer and remaps pixels separately, while oximedia-cv writes directly on the flat slice.

Pure Rust imageops::resize(Gaussian) is 40.5x slower than OpenCV pyrDown (and 2.1x slower than oximedia-cv pyr_down) because it runs a full variable-radius Gaussian resampler rather than a fixed 5-tap separable pyramid downsample.
imageproc template matching is 74.4x slower than OpenCV because it evaluates naive spatial O(W*H*w*h) sliding sums instead of FFT cross-correlation (oxipix support tracked in OXI-92).
